# Who may appear as the author or committer of a commit in this repository,
# and who may be named in a Co-authored-by: trailer.
#
# scripts/attribution-guard.sh reads this file and fails the pull request on
# anything that is not listed. Widening it is a reviewed decision — see
# CODEOWNERS — never a step on the way to a green check.
#
# One entry per line:
#
#   ADDRESS             allowed as author and as committer
#   committer:ADDRESS   allowed as committer only
#   bot:LOGIN           allowed as the GitHub account behind a commit
#   name:FULL NAME      a person whose name would otherwise read as a tool
#
# Three entries are built into the script and need no line here:
# committer:noreply@github.com (a merge made through the GitHub web UI), and
# the dependabot[bot], github-actions[bot] and renovate[bot] logins.
#
# The name beside the address is checked separately, and an allow-listed
# address does not excuse it: a commit authored by "Cursor Agent", "Claude" or
# "AI assistant" fails whatever address it carries. A real person whose name
# collides — a Jean-Claude, a Gemini — needs a `name:` line here, which is the
# only way past that rule.
#
# Delete this file and the guard still runs: it warns, falls back to the
# address built into the script, and keeps failing everybody else.
#
# Repositories made from this template: replace the address below with the
# people who actually commit here.

fschmutz@premaccess.com
